Somos CambaTech, un equipo de sistemas de Santa Cruz, Bolivia 🇧🇴. Combinamos desarrollo de software, análisis de datos e ingenio camba para resolver retos espaciales y de la Tierra. Buscamos mentes creativas (programación, diseño UI/UX, ciencia o storytelling) con ganas de innovar.

🇬🇧 Tech team from Santa Cruz, Bolivia! Passionate about coding, data, and space exploration. Looking for creative problem-solvers to build high-impact solutions together! 🚀
summary:
We developed CambaTech, an explainable crop-rotation decision support system built with React and FastAPI for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data). For any field, it ingests NASA POWER, Landsat 8/9, SMAP L4, ECOSTRESS, SRTM, SoilGrids 2.0, and NOAA ONI data to diagnose bare-soil windows and irrigation signals. It then simulates three rotations—current practice, hydro-resilient, and regenerative—over 45 years of daily climate records using FAO-56/FAO-33 water budgets, presenting interactive priority sliders and field-level explanations.

It addresses the challenge through a transparent "Clean-Pipe" pipeline that removes '-999' placeholders, masks clouds, flags irrigation bias, and quantifies soil uncertainty—showing raw versus clean data side by side instead of hiding noisy inputs.

This is important because farmers in regions like Santa Cruz, Bolivia (facing bare winter fallows) and Diamond Valley, Nevada (facing heavy irrigation demand) need trustworthy, localized evidence—and clear field-verification steps—to adopt resilient rotations without risking their livelihoods.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

CambaTech is an explainable crop-rotation decision support system that turns raw NASA Earth observation and soil data into field-specific rotation comparisons:

  1. Field Selection & Diagnosis: Users select a field via satellite map (pin, polygon, place search, or built-in scenarios like Pailón in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, and Diamond Valley, Nevada). The backend fetches multi-source climate, soil, and satellite records, classifies the ecoregion (rainfed subhumid tropics vs. irrigated cold arid basin), and diagnoses bare-soil months and irrigation signals.
  2. Clean-Pipe Telemetry: Before any simulation runs, a four-step cleaning pipeline removes NASA POWER -999 placeholders, masks Landsat cloud/shadow pixels, flags irrigation bias (dry SMAP root zone beneath green Landsat vegetation), and computes SoilGrids uncertainty (Q0.95 − Q0.05) / Q0.50.
  3. Simulation & Scoring: Using 45 years of daily NASA POWER weather, FAO-56/FAO-33 crop water budgets, USDA-SCS effective rainfall, and a daily soil-water/phenology simulation (for Southern Hemisphere annuals), the engine evaluates three rotations: Current Practice, Hydro-Resilient, and Regenerative. It outputs six 0–100 scores (water efficiency, nitrogen, erosion control, organic matter, forage value, and ease of selling) and a historical winter success KPI (e.g., how many winters out of 90 met sowing, water, and flowering-temperature thresholds).
  4. Interactive Decision Cockpit & Audit: Six priority sliders re-rank the strategies in real time (<16 ms in the browser). Each strategy includes five bilingual (EN/ES) explanation blocks generated from the field's own numbers, plus a Data Audit page showing raw vs. clean telemetry, dataset status, and CSV/JSON exports.

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • No black-box recommendations: Every score is labeled as data-driven or an agronomic rule, and users can toggle the Clean-Pipe switch in the header to see how raw satellite noise (such as cloud-contaminated pixels) distorts results.
  • Actionable uncertainty: Instead of hiding low-confidence soil maps or unmeasured local risks (like aquifer depletion or soil compaction), CambaTech surfaces SoilGrids uncertainty gauges and a checkable "verify in the field" list.
  • Resilient & accessible: Supports English and Spanish out of the box, requires no database, and includes saved scenario snapshots plus an offline frontend fallback so key case studies still work when external APIs are slow or unavailable.

What Is the Intended Impact?

CambaTech empowers farmers and agronomists—starting from two contrasting anchors, Santa Cruz, Bolivia (where bare winter fallows after soybean leave soil exposed and unproductive) and Diamond Valley, Nevada (where intensive irrigated alfalfa strains groundwater)—to evaluate climate-adapted rotations using decades of historical evidence. By showing how often a winter crop or water-saving rotation would have succeeded on their exact field and where data remains uncertain, it lowers the barrier to adopting regenerative, water-resilient practices without gambling with farm livelihoods.

Tools, Coding Languages, & Software Used

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, HTTPX, python-dotenv, and earthengine-api (Google Earth Engine).
  • Frontend: JavaScript (React), Vite, Yarn, Leaflet / React-Leaflet (interactive satellite mapping), and Recharts (telemetry and audit visualizations).
  • Data Sources & Agronomic Models: NASA POWER, Landsat 8/9 C2 L2, SMAP L4, ECOSTRESS L2T LSTE V2, SRTM 30 m, GPM IMERG (audit view), ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ONI), FAO-56 / FAO-33, Hargreaves ET0, and USDA-SCS effective rainfall.

How Is It Creative?

  • Auditability as a first-class feature: Rather than treating satellite cleaning as an invisible preprocessing step, CambaTech makes data hygiene interactive—letting users flip between raw and harmonized telemetry to witness real distortions (such as a cloud-covered December in Nevada falsely appearing as bare soil).
  • Honest "Verify in the Field" checklists: Instead of overclaiming what satellites can see, CambaTech pairs remote-sensing outputs with structured ground-truthing prompts tailored to local constraints.
  • Dual-ecoregion adaptability: A single Strategy-pattern engine seamlessly adapts from rainfed tropical winter-fallow systems to cold irrigated basins.

What Factors Did We Consider?

  • Spatial resolution limits: We evaluated and deliberately dropped 500 m MODIS ET/PET because it blurs irrigated pivots into surrounding desert, choosing 30 m Landsat + 70 m ECOSTRESS + 9 km SMAP root-zone signals instead.
  • Data gaps & placeholder traps: Long climate gaps (>5 days) are never fabricated—affected seasons are excluded and marked as no climate data—and -999 fill values are repaired and flagged.
  • Avoiding fabricated economics: Because crop prices, input costs, and yields vary by farm and year, we removed generic profit guesses and focused on physical, verifiable metrics (water deficit, net nitrogen, bare-soil months, and historical climate success rate).
  • Bilingual & offline usability: Designed in English and Spanish with cached snapshots so field demonstrations work reliably even under poor connectivity.
